Title: The living wall
Summary: Hanging plants and flowers on the school walls, to cool the building and bring in bees and butterflies.
About this project: A bare wall soaks up the sun all day and heats the rooms behind it. A living wall covers it with hanging planters full of ferns, pothos and flowers. The leaves shade the wall, the flowers feed bees and butterflies, and a grey wall turns green. Pupils plant it, water it and count the plants every month.
Next step: The next planting session adds 60 more plants.
How you can help: Adopt a planter: water it, and count it each month.
Image description: Illustration of a school wall covered in hanging plants and flowers

Title: Rainwater from the roofs
Summary: Tanks that collect the rain from our roofs, to water the plants, the farm and the pitches.
About this project: It rains a lot here, and most of it runs straight off the roofs and down the drain. Gutters now lead that rain into tanks instead. We use it to water the living wall, the farm and the pitches, so we use less mains water. Each tank has a water meter on its tap, so we know exactly how much rain we have used.
Next step: Tanks 3 and 4 go in next to the farm in December.
How you can help: Use the rainwater taps when you water the plants.
Image description: Illustration of a rainwater tank next to a building

Title: Solar panels
Summary: Solar panels on nine of the school's roofs, turning sunshine into electricity for the school.
About this project: The school already has solar panels on nine roofs, from the Senior Sports Hall to Pre-Prep. We measured them on Google Earth: about 4,810 square metres of panels. They turn sunshine into electricity that the school uses straight away, so it buys less from the grid. From the area of the panels, we estimate that they make about 4,810 kWh a day: around a third of the electricity the school uses. That is our estimate. The real meter readings will replace it.
Team: The school, with numbers from the Sustainability Group
Next step: Swap our estimate for the real meter readings.
How you can help: Spot the panels: nine roofs have them. How many can you find?
Image description: Illustration of solar panels on a school roof

Title: The school farm
Summary: The school farm is built and growing: food from the school's own soil, weighed at every harvest.
About this project: The school farm is already built and growing. Pupils help to plant it, water it and pick it, and what is picked can go to the dining hall and to food lessons. Every harvest is weighed before it leaves the farm, so the whole school can see how much food it grows.
Team: Farm Club and the dining hall team
Next step: Weigh every harvest and add it to the total.
How you can help: Come to Farm Club, or help weigh the next harvest.
Image description: Illustration of vegetable beds and a compost bin

Title: The Sustainability Dashboard
Summary: One place that shows how every project is doing, on the school website and the TVs.
About this project: Four projects, four sets of numbers, and nobody could see them together. This dashboard is the fifth project: it puts every project and every number in one place. It is shown on the school website, on the TVs around school and in the pupil portal. The Sustainability Group updates it every two weeks.
Team: The Sustainability Group, with the IT Department
Next step: The dashboard is launched in assembly.
How you can help: Have a number, a photo or some news? Tell the Sustainability Group.
